cards.text: God just spoke from the mountain, and the people were so scared they stood at a distance while Moses, Israel's leader, went into the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:18-21). Now the LORD gives Moses a message for the Israelites. It opens like this: “You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.”

cards.question: God has spoken to them straight from heaven. Next, what does He say they must not make for themselves?

answers.text: a king to rule over them
a tower that reaches the sky

cards.text: What they ARE to make is an altar of earth for their burnt offerings and peace offerings. DIRT, friend, and as a stamper who came out of a clearance bin for a quarter, that's my kind of building project.

cards.question: In every place where God causes His name to be remembered, He promises to come to them and ___ them.
If they build the altar out of stones instead, God wants those stones carefully cut and shaped with tools.

cards.text: One more altar rule: no going up to God's altar on steps, so nobody's nakedness is exposed on it. And that wraps up the altar.
Then the LORD gives Moses the ordinances to set before the people, and the first ones are about servants. If someone buys a Hebrew servant, he serves for six years.

cards.question: A Hebrew servant has served his six years. What happens in the seventh year?

answers.text: he pays a price to go free

cards.question: If a servant arrived with a wife, he has to leave her behind when he goes free.

cards.text: But if his master gave him a wife and she had children, she and the children stay with her master, and only the man goes free. Then again, the servant can declare, “I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,” and stay.

cards.question: When a servant chooses to stay, his master brings him before the judges and pierces his ear with an awl at the doorpost. How long does he serve after that?

answers.text: for the rest of his life

cards.text: A daughter sold as a servant has different rules. She doesn't go free the way the menservants do.

cards.question: If the master who chose her for himself is displeased with her, he's allowed to sell her to foreigners.

cards.text: If he chooses her for his son, he has to treat her like a daughter. And if he takes another wife, he can't cut back her food, clothing or marital rights.

cards.question: If her master doesn't provide her with food, clothing and marital rights, what happens?

answers.text: she can go free without paying
she must serve six more years
she goes back to her father's house

cards.text: Next come laws about taking a life, and they start serious: whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.

cards.question: But what if the man didn't lie in wait, and God allowed it to happen? What does God say He'll appoint for him?

answers.text: a place where he may flee
a judge who will pardon him

cards.question: A man who schemes and kills his neighbor on purpose can stay safe by holding on to God's altar.

cards.text: Some other things carry the death penalty too, like striking your father or mother, or cursing them.

cards.question: Besides striking or cursing a parent, what else carries the death penalty here?

cards.text: Now say two men are quarreling, and one hits the other with a stone or a fist. The guy lives but ends up stuck in bed, and somebody is about to get a BILL.

cards.question: Once the injured man can get up and walk around with his staff, the one who hit him must pay for his lost ___ and see that he's completely ___.
If a man strikes his servant with a rod and the servant dies by his hand, the master goes unpunished.

cards.text: But if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner isn't punished, “since the servant is his property.”
Then another case: men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman, and her child is born early. If there's no further injury, the man is fined, as her husband demands and the court allows.

cards.question: But if a serious injury does result, how is the penalty measured?
If a master strikes his servant and blinds his eye or knocks out his tooth, what must the master do?

answers.text: pay a fine to the judges

cards.text: Then comes a long run of cases about animals and property: an ox that gores, a pit left uncovered, a fire that spreads, and what's owed for theft, damage or a dowry. Borrow your neighbor's animal and it dies while he's not around? You pay for it, which means the borrowed lawnmower rule is a LOT older than lawnmowers.

Then three more with serious penalties: a sorceress must not be allowed to live, whoever lies with an animal must be put to death, and anyone who sacrifices to any god other than the LORD must be set apart for destruction.
Now God gets to how they treat other people. First up: don't exploit or oppress a foreign resident.

cards.question: Why shouldn't Israel exploit or oppress a foreign resident?

answers.text: they were foreigners in Egypt once
foreigners bring gifts to the LORD
foreigners will rule the land someday

cards.question: God says not to mistreat any widow or orphan. If someone does and they cry out to Him, He will surely hear their cry.

cards.text: And then His anger will be kindled. God says He'll kill them with the sword, so their own wives become widows and their own children fatherless.

cards.question: If they lend money to one of God's people who is poor, they must not act as a creditor or charge him ___.

cards.text: Now say you take your neighbor's cloak as collateral. God says give it back by sunset.

cards.question: Why does the neighbor's cloak have to come back by sunset?

answers.text: it's the only covering he has
the judges check it each night

cards.text: God asks, “What else will he sleep in?” and says if the man cries out, He'll hear, “for I am compassionate.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with old receipts and dust for a blanket, so GIVE THE MAN HIS CLOAK!
Then don't blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people, and don't hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. The firstborn of their sons are to be given to God.

cards.question: The firstborn of their cattle and sheep are given to God too, after staying with their mothers for ___ days.
Since they're to be God's holy people, meat from an animal mauled in the field should be offered on God's altar.

cards.text: Next up, honesty in court: don't spread a false report, and don't follow the crowd in wrongdoing when you testify in a lawsuit. So “but everybody else was doing it” is officially off the table, friend.

cards.question: In a lawsuit, a poor man should get special favor because he's poor.

cards.text: Now picture this: you spot your ENEMY's ox wandering loose. Not a stranger's ox, friend, the ox of the guy who parks in your spot every single day.

cards.question: What does God say to do with your enemy's stray ox or donkey?
If the donkey of someone who hates you falls under its load, God says that's his problem, so leave it there.

cards.text: Don't deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits, and stay far away from a false accusation. Don't kill the innocent or the just, because God says, “I will not acquit the guilty.”

cards.question: Why does God say not to accept a bribe?

answers.text: it twists what the righteous say
it costs the poor their land

cards.text: And again, don't oppress a foreign resident, because they know how it feels. Then God turns to the land: sow it and gather its produce for six years.

cards.question: In the seventh year, the land rests and lies fallow so the ___ among the people can eat from the field.
Every seventh day they must stop working, so even their ___ and their ___ can rest.
God tells them to pay close attention to everything He's said. Then what must never be heard on their lips?

cards.text: Last come the feasts: three times a year they celebrate a feast to God, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Harvest and the Feast of Ingathering, and nobody shows up empty-handed. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because God's not done talking on this mountain.
